description: We are The Young RAI, a team driven by a passion for space technology, creativity, and engineering. For NASA’s Dancing with the SARs challenge, we are ready to push boundaries, explore satellite radar data, and turn bold ideas into reality. Together, we are ready to take on the challenge and make our mark in space exploration.
summary:
FOREST-SAR is an interactive environmental monitoring platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the “Dancing with the SARs” challenge. Our project transforms real satellite radar data from NISAR, a joint NASA-ISRO mission, into accessible information about environmental changes in Honduras.

We developed FOREST-SAR, a custom scientific processing engine that compares compatible radar observations, identifies significant changes in radar backscatter, and converts the results into interactive maps, geographic zones, indicators, and analytical visualizations.

Our platform allows users to explore different time periods, investigate specific locations, and understand environmental changes without requiring specialized scientific knowledge. In our 84-day analysis, we identified 165 hectares of potential change across 98 geographic zones.

These results represent potential environmental changes, not confirmed deforestation.

FOREST-SAR aims to bridge the gap between space technology and local communities, supporting environmental research, conservation efforts, and informed decision-making. Our vision is to make satellite science accessible to everyone and contribute to a more sustainable future for Honduras.
details:
Our project, Forest SAR, is an interactive web application designed to facilitate the clear visualization and comparison of SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite imagery for the Central District in Francisco Morazán, Honduras. It is focused on analyzing land-surface changes and supporting conservation efforts. We also aim to inform and raise awareness among the general public regarding the current environmental situation and how it evolves over time. The application functions by using satellite data from the NISAR mission—which began data collection in 2025—and presenting it through an interactive map that displays data analysis for various areas.

We chose to tackle this challenge because of our strong interest in environmental issues. We believe this project will have a significant, positive impact on the entire population; forests are a shared resource that must be cared for, protected, and restored to maintain ecological balance. The data can be shared with regional authorities—such as the Institute for Forest Conservation and Development (ICF) and the Permanent Contingency Commission (COPECO)—to assist in the creation of strategic plans for the restoration or maintenance of these areas.

This project was developed using TypeScript, Python, CSS, and JavaScript, with assistance from the AI model Claude. Canva was used for the presentation. Furthermore, we conducted an exhaustive review of the theoretical framework—including all relevant references—and utilized resources provided by NASA, specifically the ASF Vertex platform, from which the analyzed maps were sourced. We believe this is a creative proposal, as it leverages advanced technology to transform information into visual maps. We have prioritized interactivity by incorporating various charts and a section dedicated to useful information.

Looking ahead, we envision an app that displays data from more locations around the world, featuring an alert system—modeled like a traffic light—to signal observed changes. We also aim to organize activities for individuals interested in serving their community through volunteer work, such as cleaning up green spaces, reforestation efforts, or collecting data and images to help counter the effects of deforestation. Furthermore, we intend to establish a collaborative network to keep the app updated.
